Redwood reported improved p50 but higher p95 in larger batches; discussed routing, KV prefix caching, quantization tradeoffs and a plan to run a 10k sample head-to-head. Security docs and pricing to be shared; next deep-dive to finalize routing/fallback playbook.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-30 16:00 PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Ortiz (Redwood SE), Sara Patel (Redwood CSM); Derek Hsu (Solstice CTO), Priya Singh (ML Eng), Tom Alvarez (Infra), Ava Romero (Product)

[00:00] Maya: hey hi everyone, thanks for joining, excited to get into the lab readout. we ran the week- three sprint tests, i'll kick it off with the topline, then Liam will walk through the traces.
[00:32] Derek: cool thanks maya. quick ask — can we keep it focused on the head-to-head with IncumbentAI? our board wants clear latency deltas before commit.
[00:48] Maya: absolutely, that's the focus today. Sara, will note follow-ups.
[00:55] Liam: ok jumping in — brief context, test harness ran 50k synthetic requests across our pilot cluster and the incumbent baseline. payloads modeled your product flows (slot-fill, short-completion ~30 tokens, and long summary ~220 tokens). we logged token-level lat, kv cache hit rates, and batch sizes.
[01:20] Priya: quick clarification, were we using your default quantization? last week there was a candidate q4 version we wanted to try.
[01:28] Liam: yes the baseline run used q8x default to mirror earlier runs; we also ran a q4f32 pass but that had slightly different output distribution so we kept primary comparison on q8x for parity.
[01:42] Tom: and infra parity — similar GPU types? we saw some differences in CPU pre-proc earlier that affected p95.
[01:50] Liam: good point. both sides used A100 equivalent instances; Redwood tests were on our dedicated pilot nodes, incubent was their managed endpoint. CPU pre-processing was consistent, though we observed more variability in network egress on the incumbent during the high-concurrency ramp.
[02:10] Maya: topline numbers: p50 improved by 12-14% across the short flows vs incumbent, throughput higher by ~22% in sustained 250 qps runs. p95 though — we saw spikes and the incumbent actually had slightly lower p95 for long completions in our window. that's what we want to unpack.
[02:40] Derek: ok that's the tension — better median but worse tail. if p95 is worse our UX suffers.
[02:48] Maya: 100% — so Liam will take us through trace-level root causes.
[02:54] Liam: jumping to the traces — showing a representative long-run [link: bench/spreadsheets/raw-traces.csv]. there's three contributing signals: 1) batch coalescing variance under bursty traffic (we had some larger-than-expected batches forming and causing headroom pressure), 2) KV-prefix cache warmup/miss storms when traffic shifts between prompt families — our prefix cache has per-model TTLs and we saw cold-start files, and 3) occasional GC pauses in the on-host process (means small but visible pauses at p95).
[03:30] Priya: when you say batch coalescing variance, is that due to continuous batching window length or because of queuing from upstream?
[03:38] Liam: mostly window policy. we have a 5ms soft-window and a 20ms hard-window — with high concurrency some requests wait to fill batches then time out and get sent in big batches. tweakable.
[03:48] Tom: can you change the window for the pilot? we can accept slightly lower throughput if it smooths p95.
[03:54] Liam: yes we can experiment — we propose two branches: reduce soft-window to 2ms and cap batch size at 8, and a second branch that enables more aggressive prefix caching (longer TTLs, prefetch on model switch).
[04:12] Maya: we rolled both in an A/B on a subset of nodes. results were promising: soft-window reduction decreased p95 for short flows by ~17% but reduced sustained throughput by about 8%. prefix caching cut cold-start misses by 60% in the traffic-shift trace.
[04:34] Derek: those are good numbers. what's the UX tradeoff? 8% throughput hit at scale means higher unit cost.
[04:42] Maya: yes — it's a classic latency vs cost tradeoff. Redwood Optimize recommendations show net unit cost up ~6% with the soft-window change but latency SLO compliance moves from 72% to 94% at p95 for short flows.
[05:00] Priya: did you try quantize changes in combination? q4 had lower memory pressure which might reduce GC pauses.
[05:08] Liam: we did a small q4 run — it reduced memory footprint by ~18%, GC events dropped but we observed a minor quality drift on a small set of semantic prompts — we're measuring eval regressions. if you prioritize tail latency we can push q4 with rerun of eval suite.
[05:28] Ava: product question — which of these tweaks can be toggled per-route? we can't afford a global throughput drop if only one route is sensitive.
[05:36] Liam: per-route routing is supported — you can pin critical routes to low-latency profile while less-sensitive ones run high-throughput config. that's where routing/fallback plays come in.
[05:46] Tom: about the network variability — earlier you mentioned incumbent had better p95 during a run window, is that possibly because they are regionally cached?
[05:55] Liam: incumbent did show steadier egress times in their managed tier because they had a multi-region edge layer in front of the model. our pilot cluster was single-region in this test. we can replicate their topology with read replicas + edge routing, but that increases complexity/cost.
[06:12] Derek: can you quantify what multi-region would do for p95?
[06:16] Maya: ballpark estimate: adding a geo-edge and small L7 cache could reduce network variance at p95 by 30-40% on long flows, but ops overhead and 3rd-party egress cost go up — we'll put an estimate in the pricing note.
[06:34] Priya: show us the raw p95 numbers for long completions again?
[06:38] Liam: sure — long completion p95 incumbent: 1.42s, Redwood baseline: 1.78s, Redwood with soft-window+prefix cache: 1.32s (but that config lowered throughput by 12% in that run).
[06:56] Derek: interesting — with the tuning you beat incumbent at long p95 but throughput hit worries me.
[07:02] Maya: understand. the trade is tunable. we can also offer a hybrid: critical endpoints pinned to tuned nodes, others on high-throughput nodes. with traffic steering you'd only pay the tuned node delta for the critical subset.
[07:18] Priya: for the head-to-head we need consistent test harnesses — can we run a 10k-sample pass using your tuned branch and their baseline at the same time? we want matched traffic patterns and seeds.
[07:26] Maya: yes — propose Thursday run with synchronized seeds. Sara will coordinate.
[07:32] Sara: noted — i'll schedule the run and share the orchestrator config.
[07:38] Tom: about KV cache — you mentioned TTLs and prefetching, can you outline the safety/consistency implications? we don't want stale context.
[07:46] Liam: prefix cache is purely read-only for previously seen cached KV entries keyed by prompt fingerprint; TTLs are short (minutes) by default to avoid staleness. prefetching just pulls the KV for the new prompt family proactively based on traffic heuristics. it's safe for inference but we can keep TTL conservative.
[08:02] Derek: security — quick run: do you support our KMS? we need BYOK and HSM, plus audit logs tied to request ids.
[08:11] Maya: yes — Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM integrations; for this pilot our dedicated nodes can be configured with a customer-managed KMS. we also produce per-request audit events and can forward logs to your SIEM. we'll share SOC2/ISO docs.
[08:28] Ava: any compliance gotchas for us as a health product? data residency?
[08:33] Maya: we can pin region and provide VPC only endpoints; for PHI workloads the Private on-prem option is available, but for this pilot regional VPC+KMS should be sufficient.
[08:45] Priya: okay — one more ML question: did you analyze tokenization differences vs incumbent? sometimes tokenizer variance causes longer tokens and higher token counts which skews per-token latency.
[08:56] Liam: yep we compared token counts across the sample set — incumbent used byte-level variant causing slightly different token splits. we normalized tokenization in the harness for fairer per-token measures; raw per-request token count delta explained about ~3% of the p50 difference earlier.
[09:14] Derek: good. back to practicalities — what's the path to a 3-month pilot contract with a dedicated slot?
[09:20] Maya: typical approach: 8-week bench + 4-week production-like soak on dedicated slot. pricing note we will send includes dedicated slot hourly with burst credits and a cap for the pilot. also include exclusivity of the capacity window so you get predictable latency.
[09:36] Tom: how fast can you spin the dedicated slot?
[09:39] Maya: from approval to slot-availability about 7 business days; if you need faster we have accelerated queues for enterprise pilots.
[09:46] Priya: we'll need SLOs in writing — p50/p95 targets for each route. can you provide a contract appendix?
[09:54] Maya: yes — we'll include SLO targets, penalties, and rollback/fallback terms in the pilot agreement.
[10:02] Liam: tangent — wanted to call out one anomaly in traces: occasional head-of-line blocking when a large batch hit the model and a small low-latency request queued behind it; we can mitigate with priority lanes (preemptive routing) for small requests.
[10:18] Priya: priority lanes sounds promising. does it require architectural changes?
[10:22] Liam: minimal — it's scheduling within the runtime. we can enable per-route priority with little disruption. we'll test in next run.
[10:30] Derek: any concerns about model quality when we change batch sizes/quantization?
[10:34] Liam: possible, that's why we ran evals. quality regressions for q4 were minor on average but some niche prompts hit lower BLEU-like metrics; we'll push your eval set against q4 and provide a diff report.
[10:48] Ava: will you share the eval diffs?
[10:50] Maya: yes, attached with the bench sheet.
[10:54] Sara: scheduling note — propose next deep-dive Wednesday 11am PT to finalize routing playbook.
[11:00] Derek: works for me.
[11:03] Priya: me too.
[11:05] Tom: yes.
[11:07] Maya: recap then: 1) run synchronized 10k head-to-head on Thursday using tuned branch; 2) Liam to deploy KV-prefetch + soft-window change on subset and report delta; 3) security docs and pricing to be shared by Maya; 4) deep-dive next Wed on routing/fallback. any other items?
[11:25] Derek: can you include an item about unit-cost per 1M tokens on tuned vs baseline?
[11:29] Maya: yes, will add cost projection to pricing note.
[11:34] Priya: one ask on metrics — include distribution histograms for batch sizes and inter-arrival times; that helped us before.
[11:40] Liam: will include those artifacts.
[11:44] Ava: small nit — the trace link earlier had some OCR-y filenames, can you add human-friendly names?
[11:49] Sara: will tidy and republish.
[11:52] Maya: great, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email with artifacts.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcript quality: speaker overlaps and some ASR errors (e.g., "K V cash" instead of KV cache, "incubent" misspellings). timestamps approximate and inserted every 20-90s to reflect key turns.
